newsitem.title: INDIA: Massive security greets Miss World in Bangalore.
newsitem.headline: Massive security greets Miss World in Bangalore.

text.p: Competitors in the Miss World beauty contest were given an armed escort from Bangalore airport to their hotel on Tuesday and hundreds of police lined the streets to ward off threatened protests.
Jeeps and vans full of rifle-toting police flanked coaches ferrying the women from 89 different countries to their hotel in the centre of the southern Indian city.

The Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), one of many groups opposing the show coming to India on grounds that it offends national culture, abandoned plans for a protest at the airport because of the massive security.
BJP legislator Suresh Kumar said police have already detained more than 40 people to prevent them from demonstrating.

Bangalore police commissioner S.C. Burman has issued prohibitory orders to head off any violence during the period November 10 to 24. These orders outlaw any protests or rallies involving more than 10 people.
Kumar said the Karnataka state government had invoked "undeclared emergency" powers.

BJP activists have threatened to lay siege to Chinnaswamy cricket stadium where Miss World will be crowned on November 23, and a militant women's group has said its members will commit suicide by taking cyanide before burning themselves to death.
"Over 40 people, mostly party workers, have been taken into preventive custody. The police is behaving as if it is the private force of the organisers," Kumar said.
The contestants flew in from the Seychelle Islands in the Indian Ocean, where the swimsuit phase of the show was held.
The organisers had shifted that part of the beauty pageant outside India to avoid upsetting local sensitivities further.
The would-be Miss Worlds were attending a carnival celebrating Bangalore on Tuesday. Two thousand guests were invited to the venue, an airforce base on the city's outskirts.

Hindi movie star Amitabh Bachchan, whose company has the license for staging this year's event, met Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Monday. Gowda, who comes from Karnataka, has been invited to attend the gala.
"It was a courtesy call," said Bachchan.
Last year the worldwide television audience for Miss World was estimated at two billion.
"Today Bangalore should have been wearing a festive look. Indian culture will be showcased to the whole world. I can't understand why some people should oppose it," Bachchan told reporters.
Bachchan also met with police commissioner Burman, who told Reuters, "We are committed to protect the contestants, the organisers and the city from acts of vandalism."
